experience.player_does: Start the game, press F2 to show or hide the world gridlines, and press Escape while playing to bring back the menu so QUIT is available.
experience.feels_like: The grid is absent by default so the cell compositions read cleanly; F2 reveals a temporary alignment aid, while Escape opens the same quiet menu over the intact world.
experience.camera: The fixed logical viewport and map presentation do not change. Returning to the menu leaves the authored world underneath unchanged.
experience.controls: F2 toggles gridlines only while the world is active. Escape returns from the world to the existing menu; PLAY dismisses it again and QUIT exits.
experience.not_this: Not a persistent graphics setting, a new pause screen, a second menu, or a change to the map data.

design_refs.why: The existing menu is the frontend surface for leaving play, and this slice makes it reachable again without inventing another screen.
The menu should feel like the same material as the world, so the existing overlay remains the only interface surface.
Grid visibility is a presentation aid around the settled cell grammar and must not alter authored cell compositions.

considered_existing.why_not: It already owns screen state, menu visibility, map drawing, and window input context, so extending it avoids a duplicate controller or overlay.
The existing Menu node and PLAY/QUIT buttons already provide the required return-and-quit surface; no scene structure needs to change.

modules.role: Own the world presentation toggles and transition back to the existing menu.
modules.why: F2 and Escape are local presentation controls that belong beside the current screen-state and drawing logic.
modules.boundary_data: Consumes InputEvent values and updates typed screen state plus a boolean grid-visibility flag; emits the existing canvas and menu visibility.

files.why: Add the default-hidden gridline state, F2 handling, and Escape transition to the existing menu while preserving map contents.

functions.why: Handle F2 and Escape after the menu controls have had first opportunity to consume input.
Keep screen-state changes and existing menu visibility synchronized for both PLAY and Escape paths.
